# v1.1.0-dev.89 — Arrow keys that work on every display

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.88`.

## The Arrow Keys Were Mostly Dead

dev.88 was named after them. On a two-monitor desk, six of the eight
combinations did nothing at all.

Four of those six were the primary display, in every direction. Windows
puts the primary at the origin, and WLM settles every arrangement back to
that. Moving the primary moved it straight back again. It moves everything
else the opposite way now. Same motion, and that one survives the settling.

The other two are real and they stay. Along the axis two displays already
share an edge on, neither can move. One direction overlaps the neighbour
and the other opens a gap. Windows keeps neither. What changed is that the
editor says so rather than doing nothing quietly:

> These displays sit side by side. Up and down are the only way they can
> move without breaking contact, which Windows will not keep.

So four of eight move, and the four that cannot say why. dev.88's own tests
asserted two of the dead cases as correct and never tested the primary at
all.

## Apply Now And Undo Disagreed

**Apply now** changes your real displays. Ctrl+Z only ever changed the
draft. Set 125%, press **Apply now**, press **Ctrl+Z**: the dropdown went
back to 100% while the monitor stayed at 125%. The readout beside it agreed
with the monitor.

The trail starts again from what is on the glass after an apply. What
undoes an apply is the 15 second Keep or Revert countdown, which is the
only thing that can put the displays back.

## Restore Defaults Asks First

It drops the display settings saved with a profile, writes that to disk on
one click, and closes the editor, taking the undo trail with it. The one
control in that dialog Ctrl+Z cannot help with. It asks now.

## Pressing ? Stopped The Keyboard

dev.88 put a display settings section in the keyboard reference, which
invited pressing **?** while you were in the display editor. Closing it
handed focus back to the sidebar. A dialog is its own window and has no
sidebar to hand it to. Focus fell nowhere. The arrow keys stopped answering
until you clicked a monitor again.

## A Smaller Download

7.7 MB smaller, and 24.9 MB less to unpack.

The library WLM uses to call Windows ships one prebuilt binary per
platform and picks its own at startup. All eighteen were riding along in a
Windows-only download: macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, three flavours of
ARM. So were 1.4 MB of its C++ sources, and the build script itself.

## Smaller Things

The **Custom resolutions** dialog was stretched to a full window with half
of it empty. It is the size of what it holds now.

In Settings, the row that adds a zoom rule squeezed two dropdowns into 319
pixels, so "Landscape (current)" was cut off mid-word with the next control
hard against it. That reads as two controls drawn on top of each other and
never was one. The row wraps instead.

The keyboard reference lists **Ctrl+Shift+Z** for redo. It has worked since
dev.88 and was written down nowhere. The hint under the monitor picture
says how far a nudge goes.

Leaving a preview of an earlier arrangement is on the undo trail. The trail
no longer claims you are looking at something you have already left.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
